cohort: All deliveries occurring over a 20-year period at a tertiary medical center, excluding multiple pregnancies, fetuses with congenital malformations, perinatal mortality cases, and women lacking prenatal care (n = 217,910)
finding: Maternal hypothyroidism during pregnancy was independently associated with an increased risk of long-term neurological morbidity in offspring, as evidenced by a higher rate of neurological-related hospitalizations.
mod_finding: The study controlled for mode of delivery as a confounding factor but did not investigate its direct association with the primary outcome.
